description: Anatomy knowledge base for the Simtack body map. One chunk per region. The retriever uses this with simple cosine similarity over a bag-of-words embedding (see app/services/anatomy_retriever.py). The LLM in /anatomy/ask uses the retrieved chunks as grounded context.

regions.text: Pain in the cranial region can involve the skull, scalp, meninges, blood vessels, and the upper cervical nerves. Common causes include tension-type headache, migraine, cluster headache, sinusitis, and high blood pressure. Red flags include sudden severe worst-ever headache, fever, neck stiffness, neurological deficits, or a headache after head injury.
suggested_questions: Is it on one side or both?
Any nausea, vomiting, or visual changes?

regions.text: Neck pain may arise from muscles, cervical spine, lymph nodes, or the thyroid. Common causes include muscle strain, cervical spondylosis, lymphadenitis from infection, and thyroiditis. Red flags include severe pain after trauma, neurological symptoms in arms, fever, or a hard fixed mass.
suggested_questions: Pain radiates to shoulders or arms?

regions.text: Chest pain can be cardiac, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, or gastrointestinal. Cardiac causes include angina and myocardial infarction. Pulmonary causes include pulmonary embolism, pneumothorax, and pneumonia. Musculoskeletal causes include costochondritis and rib injury. Red flags include crushing central chest pain, pain radiating to left arm or jaw, shortness of breath, sweating, and fainting.
red_flags: Radiation to left arm or jaw
suggested_questions: Is the pain sharp, dull, or crushing?
Does it spread to arm, jaw, or back?
Any sweating or nausea with it?

regions.text: Upper abdominal pain may come from the stomach, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, or spleen. Common causes include gastritis, peptic ulcer, gallstones, cholecystitis, pancreatitis, and hepatitis. Red flags include severe sudden pain, jaundice, vomiting blood, or black tarry stools.

structures: Right ovary and fallopian tube (in females)
regions.text: Right lower abdominal pain is classically associated with appendicitis, especially when pain starts near the navel and moves to the right lower quadrant. Other causes include right ovarian cyst, ectopic pregnancy, kidney stone, and Crohn's disease. Red flags include severe pain with fever, rigid abdomen, and fainting.
red_flags: Pain migrating from navel to right lower quadrant
suggested_questions: Did the pain start near the navel?

structures: Left ovary and fallopian tube (in females)
regions.text: Left lower abdominal pain commonly comes from the sigmoid colon, left ovary, or left ureter. Common causes include diverticulitis, constipation, ovarian cyst, ectopic pregnancy, and kidney stone. Red flags include severe pain with fever, blood in stool, or fainting.

Hip and groin pain may come from the hip joint, muscles, inguinal hernia, or pelvic structures. Common causes include hip osteoarthritis, muscle strain, inguinal hernia, and kidney stone referred pain. Red flags include inability to bear weight, severe pain after fall, or a new bulge in the groin.
suggested_questions: Can you bear weight on the leg?
Any bulge in the groin area?

regions.text: Thigh pain can come from muscles, the femur, or blood vessels. Common causes include muscle strain, contusion, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and stress fracture. Red flags include sudden swelling, calf pain, warmth, and discoloration suggestive of DVT.
suggested_questions: Any recent long travel or bed rest?

regions.text: Upper back pain often comes from muscles, thoracic spine, or referred pain from the lungs or heart. Common causes include muscle strain, thoracic spine dysfunction, and pleurisy. Red flags include pain with shortness of breath, severe pain after trauma, or neurological deficits.
red_flags: Loss of bladder or bowel control

regions.text: Lower back pain is extremely common. Causes include muscle strain, disc herniation, sciatica, kidney stones, and pyelonephritis. Red flags include loss of bladder or bowel control, numbness in the groin, severe pain after trauma, or pain with fever.
red_flags: Loss of bladder or bowel control
Numbness in groin or inner thighs
suggested_questions: Does pain radiate down the leg?

regions.text: Right arm and shoulder pain can be musculoskeletal, neurological, or referred from the neck, gallbladder, or diaphragm. Common causes include rotator cuff tendinopathy, adhesive capsulitis, cervical radiculopathy, and gallbladder referred pain. Red flags include sudden severe chest or arm pain with shortness of breath.
red_flags: Sudden chest and arm pain with shortness of breath

regions.text: Left arm and shoulder pain may be musculoskeletal, but it is also a classic site of referred cardiac pain. Chest pain radiating to the left arm is a red flag for myocardial infarction. Other causes include rotator cuff tendinopathy and cervical radiculopathy. Always rule out cardiac causes first.
red_flags: Chest pain with left arm pain
Sweating or nausea with arm pain
Sudden severe arm pain with coldness
suggested_questions: Any chest pain with the arm pain?

regions.text: Right leg and knee pain commonly comes from the knee joint, muscles, or referred pain. Common causes include meniscal tear, ligament sprain, osteoarthritis, deep vein thrombosis, and Baker's cyst. Red flags include inability to bear weight, sudden severe swelling, or a hot tender calf.
suggested_questions: Can you bear weight on the leg?

regions.text: Left leg and knee pain shares the same causes as the right side, with the addition of possible referred pain from the left lower abdomen or pelvis. Common causes include meniscal tear, ligament sprain, osteoarthritis, DVT, and kidney stone referred pain. Red flags include inability to bear weight, sudden severe swelling, or blood in urine.
suggested_questions: Can you bear weight on the leg?
